item.title: Femi Ajasa: Adeyanju, Do2dtun, others mourn late Vanguard online editor
item.description: Lawyer and human rights activist Deji Adeyanju, on-air personality Oladotun Kayode, popularly known as Do2dtun, and former presidential aide Bashir Ahmad are among public figures who have mourned the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s online editor, Olufemi Ajasa, who died on Sunday at the age of 44. The deceased’s death was announced by Vanguard Media Limited, which said he passed away at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital after a brief illness. In a statement, the newspaper’s editor, Eze Anaba, described Ajasa’s death as a major loss to the organisation and the journalism profession, noting his contributions to the growth of its digital operations and online journalism. Reacting to his death on Tuesday, Adeyanju, in a tribute shared on Facebook, described Ajasa as a longtime friend and brother, saying they shared a close relationship for nearly two decades. He wrote, “We shared a close friendship for nearly two decades, and losing such a trusted ally to the cold hands of death is truly heartbreaking. My heartfelt condolences go out to his family and the entire Vanguard Newspaper team for this irreparable loss. I will always hold onto the wonderful memories of our travels together and the countless ideas we exchanged. “The kindhearted never truly die—they live on in our hearts forever. May God comfort his loved ones, and may his gentle soul rest in perfect peace.” Do2dtun, who worked with Cool FM, also expressed grief over Ajasa’s death in a post on X, describing him as an exceptional journalist who maintained professionalism in his work. He said Ajasa refused to accept money to publish a blackmail-related story against him, adding that the journalist declined attempts to persuade him to run the report. “Femi Ajasa, your loss broke me. You are an amazing journalist, never biased and you were a professional to the core. You never used your pen for evil,” he wrote. Similarly, Bashir Ahmad, a former media aide to ex-President Muhammadu Buhari, said he had known Ajasa since 2016 and valued his professionalism, dedication to journalism and warmth towards people. In a post on X, Ahmad said the journalist’s death was a painful loss to his family, friends and the Nigerian media industry. “I have had the privilege of knowing and sharing a friendship with Mr. Ajasa since 2016. Over the years, I came to appreciate his professionalism, dedication to journalism and the warmth with which he related with people. His passing is a painful loss, not only to his family and loved ones but also to the Nigerian media industry, where he made meaningful contributions,” he wrote. Director of New Media and Strategic Communication of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Theo Aguda, also described Ajasa as a friend and brother. “In Femi, I have lost a dear friend and brother. item.title: Kano gov Yusuf invites marriage applicants after divorce from Kwankwaso’s daughter
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf Kano State Governor, Abba Yusuf, has invited women interested in marrying him to apply. The governor made the announcement on Monday while addressing pensioners at the Kano Government House. Yusuf said he had accepted the decision to remain with one wife for now but was open to marrying again. “Some days ago, I was being forced to become a being with one wife. I want to thank the good people of Kano who advised me to keep two wives, but for now, I have accepted one wife,” he said. He also confirmed that the divorce process had been initiated. “The governor has agreed to divorce her. Is it not the paper (notice of marriage dissolution)? The governor has issued that,” he said. He disclosed that he had directed the Commissioner for Information to place advertisements on radio stations and social media platforms to invite women interested in becoming his wives. The development comes after Zainab Musa Kwankwaso, daughter of former Kano State Governor and Yusuf’s former political godfather, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, filed for divorce at the Upper Area Court in Gudu, Abuja, on Saturday. item.title: NDLEA busts transnational cocaine syndicate, arrests 8 members in Lagos, Kano
item.description: …Couriers on Nigeria-Niger-Libya-Europe Trip Excrete 634 Pellets in Custody By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said on Tuesday that its operatives have dismantled a transnational drug trafficking cartel that moves cocaine from Lagos through Kano and across the desert via the Republic of Niger and Libya to Europe. The spokesman of the agency, Femi Babafemi, in a statement said, “As a result, eight members of the syndicate were arrested in well-coordinated intelligence-guided operations in Lagos and Kano. “All eight suspects who were nabbed between Friday 30th and Saturday 31st October 2026 were drug mules who had swallowed cocaine pellets, excreting a total of 634 wraps weighing 13.795 kilograms over several days in custody. Babafemi said, “The operation began on Friday, 30th October, when operatives of a Special Operations Unit of the Agency arrested the first suspect, 57-year-old Okwudiba Ifeanyichukwu Damian, at Nice Touch Hotel, Ago Palace, Okota, Lagos. “He later excreted 74 wraps of cocaine weighing 1.650 kg. “The next day, Saturday, 31st October, four more members of the cartel were stopped at the MM2 Terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, as they prepared to board a flight to Kano. “They are Jackson Ahamefule, 43, who excreted 90 wraps weighing 1.950 kg; Nwafor Osita Emmanuel, 47, who excreted 85 wraps weighing 1.750kg; Marcel Nnabuike, 38, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.655kg; and Onyenwuba Ignatius, 44, who excreted 75 wraps weighing 1.650kg. “The five mules arrested in Lagos excreted 399 wraps of cocaine weighing 8.655 kg in all. Intelligence from the Lagos operation showed that other members of the cartel had already travelled to Kano, where NDLEA officers at the Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport (MAKIA) were swiftly mobilised to intercept them at the arrival hall of the domestic terminal of the Kano airport. As a result, three other members of the syndicate, namely Chinweike Ephraim Ifechukwu, 48; Edezuno John Nwaorji, 45; and Chukwudi Chinaka, 31, were identified and arrested. A body scan showed that all three had swallowed drugs, after which they were placed under excretion observation. Over the following days, Ifechukwu excreted 85 pellets of cocaine weighing 1.853 kg; Nwaorji expelled 80 pellets weighing 1.752 kg, while Chinaka excreted 70 pellets with a total weight of 1.535 kg. The suspects said they had planned to travel by road from Kano through the Republic of Niger to Libya, with Europe as the final destination for the drugs. item.title: PR cannot cover bad leadership, global experts warn
item.description: By John Alechenu Global public relations experts have warned governments and corporate organisations to stop using PR, propaganda or strategic messaging to hide leadership failures. Trust, they said, cannot be bought with publicity. It must be earned through integrity, accountability and actions that match promises. The warning came at a session on Ethical Leadership and Trust in a Divided World at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja, organised by the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management and the Nigeria Institute of Public Relations. The panel featured the Alliance’s regional council chairs for Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa, Middle East and South Asia, and North America. It was moderated by Chimdi Neliaku, Chair of the NIPR Young Professionals Hub. For Europe, Global Alliance Vice President and Chair of its European Regional Council, Silvia Arto, said ethical leadership is shown in personal conduct, not public declarations. “To me, ethical leadership is lead by example. It’s walk the talk. It’s integrity,” she said, adding that integrity meant doing what was right even when nobody was watching. Trust, she warned, takes years to build but can be destroyed within seconds, particularly through social media. “Trust and ethical leadership, personal leadership, is built through actions, not declarations,” Arto said. She urged professionals to promote transparency, media literacy and dialogue while combating misinformation, propaganda and misuse of artificial intelligence. Citing the European Union’s AI Act, she called for human accountability and ethical guidelines for emerging technologies. Arto also invoked Yoruba wisdom, declaring: “Character is beauty.” From Asia-Pacific, Chair Jaffri Osman said effective leadership requires more than intellectual intelligence. Emotional and social intelligence matter just as much in building relationships across diverse communities. “Trust is built by leaders who understand beyond IQ. They have to understand EQ and SQ,” he said. Using Malaysia’s Sarawak region as an example of multicultural coexistence, Osman said professionals must understand local cultures, traditions and relationships to influence communities responsibly. “When we talk about influence, when we talk about communication, and when we talk about going ahead effectively in ethical communication, we must go respect,” he said. For Africa, Chair Ms Irene Lungu Chipili identified political messaging, democratic competition and misinformation as major threats to public confidence. She questioned whether citizens could trust messages from political parties and governments, arguing that the credibility of the messenger was as important as the information. item.title: Jonathan Warns Against Ethnic Rivalry, Political Intolerance Ahead Of General Elections
item.description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned that the rising tide of political intolerance, thuggery, and deliberate stoking of ethnic rivalries pose a severe threat to Nigeria’s national existence and stability ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎Speaking at a high-level peace and security conference hosted by the Goodluck Jonathan Foundation in Abuja, Jonathan stressed that upcoming electoral cycles must not become catalysts for destructive division. He urged political leaders and citizens alike to prioritise national unity, democratic values, and responsible leadership over narrow partisan ambitions. Former President Goodluck Jonathan and others at a high-level peace and security conference in Abuja on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The former president also urged Nigerians to treat the upcoming 2027 general elections as a critical opportunity to choose credible leadership at both state and federal levels, prioritising competence over ambition. He warned that undermining national cohesion for political ambition poses a severe danger to the country’s existence. “Nothing could be more dangerous to our national existence than the deliberate encouragement of ethnic rivalry. We must never allow political ambition to undermine the bonds that hold us together as one nation and one country, both at the national level and at the state level”, he said. The post Jonathan Warns Against Ethnic Rivalry, Political Intolerance Ahead Of General Elections appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Reps hail unanimous approval of State Police by 36 assemblies
item.description: The House of Representatives has welcomed the approval by all 36 State Houses of Assembly of the proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Services. The House described the unanimous endorsement as a significant milestone in the constitutional amendment process, saying it represents 100 per cent approval by the state legislatures and exceeds the constitutional requirement of at least 24 State Houses of Assembly under Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution. The House Spokesman, Rep. Akin Rotimi Jr., disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. According to the statement, the approval was confirmed by the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, who said the bill had satisfied the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission. Ogunlana, in a statement issued on Monday, November 16, explained that the bill had earlier met the requirements for transmission but that the leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay to allow for broader national consensus and engagement with all states. He said: “The Bill had long satisfied all the constitutional and administrative requirements for transmission as prescribed by the Constitution and the Acts Authentication Act Cap. A2, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004, but the Leadership of the National Assembly directed a brief delay of transmission to allow for broader national consensus and engagement of all the States of the Federation.” The Clerk further confirmed that following the completion of the verification process by his office, the bill was ready for transmission to President Bola Tinubu for assent. He described the unanimous endorsement as an unprecedented demonstration of cooperation between the National Assembly and the State Houses of Assembly, as well as between the executive arms of government at federal and state levels. The House of Representatives acknowledged the collective efforts of both chambers of the National Assembly and all 36 State Houses of Assembly in advancing the proposed constitutional reform. It particularly recognised the work of the House Committee on Constitution Review, chaired by the Deputy Speaker, Benjamin Kalu. The House also commended the 36 state governors, speakers and members of the State Houses of Assembly, as well as other stakeholders, for their cooperation and commitment to the proposed reform of policing in Nigeria. It said the unanimous approval marked an important step towards strengthening the country’s security architecture, improving responses to local security challenges and advancing the establishment of State Police Services. The House added that the development would provide a foundation for the National Assembly to complete and transmit the remaining Sixth Constitution Alteration Bills to the State Houses of Assembly for consideration. item.title: NNPC confirms Lagos filling station fire contained
item.description: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC Ltd) has confirmed that a fire outbreak at an affiliated filling station along Ekoro-Ajasa Road, in Alimosho Local Government Area of Lagos State, has been contained. The company said preliminary information indicated that no fatalities or injuries were recorded in the incident, which occurred on Monday, November 16, 2026. NNPC disclosed this in a statement issued by its Chief Corporate Communications Officer, Andy Odeh, in Abuja. The company acknowledged the fear and distress caused by the incident among residents, customers and businesses in the area, expressing sympathy with those whose properties or livelihoods might have been affected. NNPC commended the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service and other emergency responders for containing the fire and preventing further damage. It said its Retail, Health, Safety and Environment teams, alongside the management of the affected filling station, were reviewing the cause of the incident. The company assured residents that the safety of customers, employees and neighbouring communities remained a priority. It added that it would support relevant authorities and the management of the affiliated filling station in addressing the incident, promising to provide further updates as verified information became available. The post NNPC confirms Lagos filling station fire contained appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria’s Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa, has said the United States is providing real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training to the Nigerian military to track and target terrorist leaders ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to Reuters, Musa disclosed this on Monday during a briefing with journalists, saying the improved intelligence support had strengthened the military’s ability to identify and strike militant targets. The minister said Nigerian troops had killed several terrorist and bandit leaders in overnight operations in the Northwest and Northeast, adding that the military was conducting almost daily operations with improved intelligence. “We took out a lot of the bandit leaders and the terrorists themselves,” Musa said. He said Nigeria and the United States had continued to expand their security cooperation as the country battles Islamist insurgencies in the North-East, armed banditry in the North-West and kidnapping gangs across the country. Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was expecting additional military helicopters from the United States and Italy to strengthen its operational capacity. On preparations for the 2027 general elections, the defence minister said security agencies were intensifying intelligence-led operations to prevent violence before, during and after the polls. He said authorities were also monitoring the use of Starlink satellite internet services, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones by militant groups, while working with US authorities to disrupt their financing networks. Musa further disclosed that Nigeria had reached a five-kilometre cross-border right-of-pursuit arrangement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad, allowing troops to pursue terrorists and bandits across border areas. The arrangement is aimed at restricting the movement of armed groups that exploit porous borders to escape security operations. The minister also warned that Islamic State Sahel was seeking to recruit criminal gangs in North-West Nigeria, raising concerns that largely profit-driven bandit groups could develop into ideologically driven insurgent organisations similar to the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP). According to him, militants and bandits have continued to exploit dense forests and porous borders with Niger and Benin to evade security forces after carrying out attacks. However, he said improved surveillance had strengthened the military’s ability to track armed groups through difficult terrain and restricted their freedom of movement. “We don’t want them to develop that capacity,” Musa said. “We’re blocking the logistics and taking them out from within Nigeria.” The post 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Obi highlights institutional reforms during Anambra tenure
item.description: Former Anambra State Governor and the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has highlighted the institutional reforms undertaken by his administration, saying rebuilding the machinery of government was essential to achieving sustainable development. Obi disclosed this on Tuesday in the second instalment of his series, titled Nigerians, Go and Verify, published on his X handle. In the article, titled Building the Institutions of the State, the former governor explained that his administration prioritised strengthening government institutions under the Anambra Integrated Development Strategy, ANIDS, before embarking on broader development projects. He said his administration was guided by the principles of character, competence, capacity and compassion, adding that a development vision could not succeed without strong institutions to implement it. According to him, the physical and administrative structures of governance were in deplorable condition when he assumed office, making it necessary to rebuild institutions across the executive, legislature, judiciary, civil service and local government system. Restoring the seat of government Obi said his administration rebuilt, re-equipped and furnished the Government House in Awka after it was vandalised and burnt in 2004. He added that the Governor’s Lodge in Amawbia was rehabilitated, while a new Governor’s Lodge was constructed in Onitsha to strengthen executive presence and facilitate governance across the state’s major administrative and commercial centres. Strengthening the legislature and judiciary The former governor said his administration also rehabilitated the Anambra State House of Assembly Complex in Awka and provided vehicles to lawmakers to facilitate the discharge of their legislative responsibilities. He said the judiciary was equally strengthened through the provision of brand-new vehicles to High Court judges, which he described as the first of its kind in the state’s history. Obi also said vehicles were provided to magistrates for the first time since the creation of Anambra State. He explained that the interventions were aimed at improving mobility, strengthening the administration of justice and enabling judicial officers to perform their duties more effectively. Rebuilding the civil service On the civil service, Obi said many Ministries, Departments and Agencies, MDAs, operated from scattered rented apartments before his administration, while civil servants lacked a centralised and decent working environment. He said the arrangement undermined administrative coordination, efficiency and the dignity of public service. To address the situation, he said his administration constructed the two-phase Chief Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex, comprising Blocks 1 and 2, to bring the MDAs together and provide civil servants with a more conducive working environment. item.title: FG introduces NIN-linked verification system for domestic air passengers
item.description: The Federal Government has introduced a biometric passenger verification system linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) for domestic air travel, in a move aimed at strengthening airport security and curbing identity fraud. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday after unveiling the Airport Passenger Verification System, known as V-PASS, at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos. Keyamo said the system would make it mandatory for passengers on domestic flights to verify their identities using their NIN before boarding. He explained that the technology was designed to eliminate cases of passengers travelling with fake identities, as well as address touting and ticket racketeering at airports. According to him, the biometric identity verification system would enhance passenger processing, strengthen airport security and provide a faster and more seamless travel experience. The minister said the project was executed through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement. He was accompanied at the unveiling by the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Mrs Olubunmi Kuku; Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh; and other senior FAAN officials. Keyamo said he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to give all airlines operating in the country until December 31 to integrate with the system. He clarified that the verification system was designed exclusively for domestic flights. The post FG introduces NIN-linked verification system for domestic air passengers appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu: Nigerians can access ₦100m mortgages at 9.75%
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said eligible Nigerians can access mortgage loans of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent under the Federal Government’s ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF). Tinubu, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Tuesday, said the initiative was designed to expand access to affordable, long-term housing finance and help more Nigerians become homeowners. He explained that beneficiaries could repay the loans over a period of up to 20 years, with an initial deposit of 10 per cent. Illustrating the arrangement, the President said a Nigerian seeking to purchase a house worth ₦10 million would need an initial deposit of ₦1 million and could repay approximately ₦85,400 monthly over 20 years. According to him, more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have so far accessed ₦160 billion in mortgages through MREIF. Tinubu said the Federal Government had also strengthened the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN), through which eligible Nigerians could access housing loans of up to ₦50 million at six per cent interest, with repayment periods of up to 30 years. He added that contributors to pension schemes could qualify to use up to 25 per cent of their retirement savings towards the initial deposit, while married applicants could submit joint applications with their spouses to improve their chances of accessing higher loan amounts. The President also highlighted the role of the Family Homes Fund in providing affordable housing for Nigerians who cannot afford mortgage arrangements. He said the fund had delivered more than 53 social homes for vulnerable and underserved households. Tinubu further disclosed that the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme was targeting 77,400 affordable homes across the country. According to him, 100 free homes had been delivered to widows in Kaduna, while another 50 were provided to wives of fallen military personnel in Ibadan. He added that more than 15,000 housing units were under construction nationwide through the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme. The President stressed that access to the housing initiatives should be based on eligibility rather than political connections or religious affiliation. “You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities,” he said. Tinubu maintained that the programmes were open to Nigerians who met the stipulated requirements, irrespective of their location or beliefs. He said providing opportunities for hardworking Nigerians to own homes and secure their families’ future remained an important objective of his administration’s economic reforms. The post Tinubu: Nigerians can access ₦100m mortgages at 9.75% appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Enugu Assembly passes bill limiting rent increase to 2%
item.description: … Landlords can only review rent after four years By Chinedu Adonu The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to protect tenants from arbitrary rent increases by restricting landlords to a maximum two per cent increment every four years. The bill, which scaled its third reading on Tuesday, also provides for a maximum 10 per cent rent increase where a landlord has undertaken reasonable renovation of the property. Its passage followed the consideration of a report presented by a joint House committee comprising the Committees on Housing and Investment, Public Petition, Ethics and Privileges, and Judiciary. The motion for consideration of the report was moved by the member representing Nkanu West Constituency, Hon. Iloabuchi Aniagu, and seconded by the member representing Awgu North Constituency, Rt. Hon. Jane Eneh. Presenting the report, Chairman of the Committee, Rt. Hon. Okey Mbah, who represents Nkanu East Constituency, said the proposed amendment followed extensive consultations with relevant stakeholders. Mbah described the legislation as a major intervention in landlord-tenant relations, saying it was designed to address the exploitation of tenants and ease the burden of securing accommodation in the state. “This bill will subside over 60 per cent of what residents used to pay while trying to secure accommodation,” he said. Following the presentation, the House dissolved into the Committee of the Whole to consider the report alongside the bill before its eventual passage. The Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Uche Ugwu, described the legislation as part of the good governance initiatives of the present administration, saying it would give tenants in the state a new lease of life. The bill, titled A Bill for a Law to Amend the Landlord and Tenant Second Amendment Bill, Cap 101, Revised Laws of Enugu State 2024, House Bill No. 3, 2025, passed second reading on March 11, 2026, and subsequently underwent a public hearing on March 26, 2026. With its passage by the Assembly, the bill now awaits the assent of Governor Peter Mbah before it can become law. The post Enugu Assembly passes bill limiting rent increase to 2% appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Car washer jailed seven years for stealing customer’s Lexus SUV in Enugu
item.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—-A 36-year-old car washer, Adah Martins Pius, has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment for stealing a customer’s Toyota Lexus 330 SUV in Enugu State. The Enugu State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Daniel Ndukwe. According to the statement, Pius stole the black Lexus SUV on November 5, 2026, after it was entrusted to him by its owner for washing at Fourth Dimension, Enugu. Rather than wash and return the vehicle, the convict, a native of Ugep in Yakurr Local Government Area of Cross River State, allegedly absconded with it and fled to his hometown. Following a complaint by the vehicle’s owner, operatives of the New Haven Police Division deployed technical intelligence to track down and arrest him in Cross River State. The stolen SUV was subsequently recovered on November 11, 2026. The police said Pius was arraigned before the Enugu North Magistrate Court on November 16, 2026, on a one-count charge of stealing. He pleaded guilty to the charge and was convicted and sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment by the court. The Command commended the operatives involved in the investigation and arrest, as well as the court for the speedy dispensation of justice. It reiterated its commitment to sustaining efforts to rid Enugu State of criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents and their property. item.title: Ikeja LG chairman mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Executive Chairman of Ikeja Local Government, Comrade Akeem Olalekan Dauda, popularly known as AKOD, has commiserated with Vanguard Media Limited, the family and associates of its late Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa. Dauda described Ajasa’s death as a painful loss to the media industry and the journalism profession. Ajasa, aged 44, reportedly died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. In a condolence message, the council chairman said the late journalist’s dedication, professionalism and contributions to the growth of digital journalism would remain part of his enduring legacy. He described Ajasa as a committed media professional whose career across several reputable media organisations reflected his passion for journalism, pursuit of excellence and determination to contribute to the evolving media landscape. Dauda particularly commiserated with the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the immediate family of the deceased, as well as his friends and professional colleagues. He urged them to take solace in the impactful life and professional contributions of the late journalist. “Take solace in the impactful life and professional contributions of the late Ajasa, whose passing at the age of 44 is a painful reminder of the fragility of life,” he stated. The council chairman also prayed that Almighty God would comfort the bereaved family, grant them the strength to bear the loss and give the deceased eternal rest. item.title: 2027: Ijaw people support Tinubu’s re-election, Diri declares
item.description: ..Commends Tompolo-led campaign movement …Group donates 25 buses for campaign By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, has declared that the majority of Ijaw people support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Diri said he was confident that the Ijaw nation would give Tinubu overwhelming support in the election, describing the President and the people of the Niger Delta as being in the same political boat. The governor spoke during a rally organised by the High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, led PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital. He said the Ijaw people, being experienced mariners and navigators, would ensure that the political boat sailed to victory. Diri listed the ongoing construction of the second phase of the Nembe-Brass Road, tax waivers granted to the state’s independent power plant and the coastal highway project among the benefits he said Bayelsa had received under Tinubu’s administration. He also commended Tompolo for his commitment to Tinubu’s re-election campaign, describing his involvement in a nationwide presidential campaign as a source of pride to the Ijaw people. “This is the first time an Ijaw son is carrying a presidential campaign across states on this scale. As a people who have over the years talked about injustice and recognition, we are proud of Tompolo,” he said. The governor also thanked the movement’s leader for donating 25 vehicles to support the President’s campaign in Bayelsa. Diri, while dismissing claims that a particular political party was the Ijaw party, said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was the party to which he, Tompolo and other prominent Ijaw people belonged. According to him, “The real Ijaw party in Nigeria is the APC, to which I, as Governor-General of the Ijaw nation, Tompolo and other prominent Ijaw sons and daughters belong.” Earlier, the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Kestin Pondi, who represented Tompolo, said the visit was to inaugurate the Bayelsa State chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement. Pondi acknowledged Diri’s role in the President’s re-election campaign and expressed confidence in the collaboration between the governor and the movement. He described Tinubu as a bold and courageous leader who had prioritised Nigeria in his reform agenda, arguing that the President deserved another term to consolidate the gains of his administration. item.title: Simon Ekpa freed from Finnish custody, Ejimakor announces
item.description: Nigerian-born separatist leader, Simon Ekpa, has been freed from custody in Finland, according to a Nigerian lawyer, Aloy Ejimakor. Ejimakor disclosed this on his Facebook page on Tuesday, saying he received confirmation of Ekpa’s release from his close friend and ally, Dr David Matsanga. “ Mazi SIMON EKPA has just been FREED. His close friend and ally, Dr David Matsanga, confirmed it to me just minutes ago during our telephone conversation,” Ejimakor wrote. The announcement comes amid earlier reports that Ekpa was scheduled to be released on November 17, 2026. His legal support team had previously confirmed the date, following the circulation of a viral video purportedly showing him walking out of a building said to be the facility where he was being detained. Ekpa, 41, had been in Finnish custody since November 2024. He was convicted in September 2025 by the Päijät-Häme District Court over his alleged involvement in activities linked to armed separatist groups operating in southeastern Nigeria. item.title: $4.5m car theft: Canadian police arrest eight Nigerians, four others
item.description: By Matthew Johnson Peel Regional Police, Canada, has arrested eight Nigerians among 12 suspects following the dismantling of a transnational auto theft syndicate allegedly shipping stolen luxury vehicles to West Africa. The suspects, who are facing a combined 231 criminal charges, were nabbed after detectives with the Commercial Auto Crime Bureau recovered 96 stolen high-value vehicles, predominantly luxury sport utility vehicles, SUVs, and pickup trucks valued at approximately $4.5 million. In a video posted on its official X (formerly Twitter) handle on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, the Peel Regional Police disclosed that the investigation, code-named Project Cadetta, was launched in March 2026 in collaboration with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA). According to the police, the operation initially focused on a warehouse in Brampton, Ontario, which served as a primary staging facility where stolen vehicles with altered Vehicle Identification Numbers (re-VINed) were concealed inside shipping containers destined for West African markets through Canadian ports. Further investigations uncovered a broader criminal network operating across the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) and surrounding jurisdictions. Police alleged that the syndicate was spearheaded by five principal suspects—all bearing Nigerian names who coordinated the theft, movement, and overseas export of the vehicles. They were identified as Odewale Abraham (57), Tosin Oyebade (45), Oluyemi Sodade (51), and Oluwaseyi Bameke (39), all of Toronto, alongside Stanley Udeh (46) of Brampton. Seven other suspects accused of facilitating the racket through transportation, container movements, and managing loading sites were identified as Gbolahan Babatunde (29) of Vaughan; Olushola Oke (42) of Toronto; Kenneth Okafor (58) of no fixed address; Karamveer Singh (26) of Brampton; Darryl Davance (25) of Saint Jerome, Quebec; Henrik Gancz (57) of no fixed address; and Jaspreet Singh (25) of no fixed address. Following a series of coordinated search warrants and arrests, nine of the accused were charged and released with future court dates, while three were held for bail hearings and subsequently granted release. Canadian authorities disclosed that some of the charged suspects may be referred to the CBSA for immigration enforcement action, including possible deportation from Canada, upon the conclusion of their criminal trials. Meanwhile, arrest warrants have been issued for two additional suspects still at large: 32-year-old Steven Gyamfi and a 16-year-old minor from Hamilton whose identity is protected under Canada’s Youth Criminal Justice Act. Commenting on the breakthrough, Deputy Chief of Peel Regional Police, Nick Milinovich, vowed that the force would sustain its clampdown on organised crime syndicates. “Organised auto theft is a predatory business model run by transnational syndicates that terrorise families and fund broader criminal enterprises. item.title: Singapore In Damage Control After Nvidia Scandal Exposes China Loophole
item.description: Singapore is working to maintain its reputation as a trusted business hub, tainted by allegations that Chinese companies had exploited it to gain access to top-end AI chips despite US export restrictions. A widening scandal sparked by an affair between Jensen Huang, until recently head of US chip titan Nvidia, and a suspected Chinese spy has spotlighted the city-state’s position as a global crossroads for the advanced semiconductors that power artificial intelligence. This screengrab from video footage by CTI obtained via AFPTV on November 9, 2026 shows Alice Huang (R), a Chinese executive linked to the data centre company called Megaspeed, attending a dinner hosted by Nvidia’s chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang (L in black back facing camera) at a restaurant in Taipei on May 22, 2025, during Computex, the island’s top tech expo. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP The United States on Monday moved to close a loophole in its controls — which it says protect national security — on the export of powerful AI chips to China. The new US rules crack down on illicit chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres full of advanced Nvidia chips in third countries, often in Southeast Asia. It follows explosive reports of Huang’s affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed International, which Washington is investigating for the alleged transfer of Nvidia chips to China in circumvention of US rules. The scandal “is obviously not a good look for Singapore”, Chong Ja Ian, a political scientist with the National University of Singapore, told AFP. Singapore is also probing what Megaspeed was up to, but Chong said the city-state must strengthen regulatory oversight to avoid the perception of “systemic issues”. Map of Singapore The Nvidia case may make it harder “to maintain the reputation of being a clean business hub by simply dealing with individual cases, rather than putting more stringent regulations and laws in place”, he said. Some US officials also reportedly believe that Alice Huang, no relation to the leather jacket-clad Jensen, was spying for Beijing. Caught in crossfire? Singapore said it was carefully studying the new US measures, which require data centres worldwide to hold a US licence to provide a large volume of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, or other places under US arms embargoes. A US licence will also be needed to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the sensitive components. “We take our international reputation seriously,” the Singaporean government said. item.title: “I Remain Senior Pastor”: Jimmy Odukoya Dismisses Fountain Of Life Removal
item.description: Pastor Jimmy Odukoya has rejected an announcement purporting to remove him as Senior Pastor of The Fountain of Life Church, insisting that he remains the ministry’s substantive leader and Chairman of its Board of Trustees. In a counter-statement issued on Tuesday, 17 November 2026, Odukoya’s camp dismissed an earlier press release from a faction of the Board of Trustees, describing the purported removal as unconstitutional and invalid. “We categorically reject this purported decision and wish to clarify that the announcement does not represent a constitutionally valid decision of the Board of Trustees of The Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church,” the rebuttal read. Rival Claims Over Constitutional Authority The rebuttal directly challenges a statement issued earlier on Tuesday following a 16 November meeting, in which a group of trustees claimed to have withdrawn recognition of Odukoya as senior pastor over an alleged December 2021 succession video by late founder Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, alongside concerns surrounding Odukoya’s recent remarriage. In response, Odukoya’s camp alleged that the removal notice was issued by a breakaway group calling itself “Concerned Members of the Board” whose members had already been asked to step down months earlier. “It is important to place on record that, as far back as 14 March 2026, these Trustees were formally called upon to resign from the Board on account of their repeated and flagrant violations of the Church’s Constitution and its founding principles and objectives,” the counter-statement asserted, adding that one trustee subsequently resigned after receiving the notice. Maintaining that his September 2023 appointment was unanimously approved by the Board following his father’s passing in August 2023, the statement insisted that no valid constitutional process had removed him from office. “For the avoidance of doubt, Pastor Jimmy Odukoya remains the duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees of The Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church,” it stated. “The Constitution remains the governing instrument of the Church. No individual or group of individuals can substitute their preferences for the express provisions of that Constitution.” Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and his wife, Pastor Mo Odukoya, during her official introduction to the congregation at The Fountain of Life Church in Lagos on November 1, 2026. (Photo: instagram.com/iamthatpj/) The 2021 Video Claim And Remarriage Backlash Earlier on Tuesday, the opposing Trustees alleged that Odukoya’s 2023 appointment was made in error because a witnessed December 2021 recording, filmed by Odukoya himself at his late father’s request, was withheld when the board enquired about succession instructions. According to those Trustees, the late founder named a different successor in the video and designated Odukoya solely as an administrative assistant and head of the youth church. item.title: Reno Omokri mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
item.description: Former presidential aide and Nigeria’s Ambassador to Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua, Bemigho Reno Omokri, has mourned the passing of Vanguard Newspapers’ Online Editor, Mr Femi Ajasa, describing his death as a loss to Nigerian journalism. Omokri, in a condolence message posted on his Facebook page on Tuesday, said Ajasa embodied the Omoluabi principle and demonstrated professionalism, ethical conduct and commitment to excellence in journalism. He said he had known the late journalist personally, recalling that Ajasa extended a hand of fellowship to him during his lifetime. “On behalf of my family and I, please accept my condolences on the death of your staff member, Online Editor Femi Ajasa. “I knew Mr Ajasa, and he truly embodied the Omoluabi principle. He extended his right hand of fellowship to me in his lifetime, and it is a sad day for Nigerian journalism that he is no more,” he said. The ambassador described Ajasa as a model of high-level reporting, drawing a comparison between his journalistic standards and those of Vanguard’s founder, Mr Sam Amuka. He also credited Ajasa’s dedication to journalism and pursuit of excellence with contributing to Vanguard’s prominence in online publishing. According to him, the late editor’s professional ethics and insight had created a vacuum that would be difficult to fill. “The vacuum that Mr Ajasa’s passing has created will be difficult to fill because of the ethics and insight he brought to his job,” Omokri said. He prayed for the repose of Ajasa’s soul and asked that his memory remain blessed. “May his soul rest in peace and his memory be forever blessed,” he added. The post Reno Omokri mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Drones Behind Nearly 75% Of Civilian Deaths This Year In Sudan War — UN
item.description: Drones caused nearly three quarters of all the verified civilian fatalities this year in the war in Sudan, the UN said Tuesday. The war between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) erupted in April 2023 and is estimated to have killed more than 200,000 people in total. The conflict has forced more than 13 million to flee their homes, creating the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis, according to aid groups. A young displaced Sudanese girl reacts after spending a night with others in Gedaref city, eastern Sudan, on December 26, 2025, after the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) took control of the Heglig area in western Sudan. (Photo by AFP) Out of 2,230 civilian deaths confirmed by the UN human rights office OHCHR to have occurred this year between January and the end of October, more than 1,630 were a result of drone attacks, it said on Tuesday. Drone attacks have “eclipsed the use of other tactics and weaponry”, it said, adding that the full civilian casualty figures are likely to be higher. A Sudanese woman who fled El-Fasher sits next to aid she received at the Al-Afad camp for displaced people in the town of Al-Dabba, northern Sudan, on November 25, 2025. (Photo by Ebrahim HAMID / AFP) Both warring parties have increasingly relied on drones capable of striking targets hundreds of kilometres away. In a report on the human rights situation in Sudan, OHCHR said the first six months of the year were marked by an “unmistakable increase in drone strikes against civilians and civilian objects”. The use of drones has now become “one of the defining features of the conflict”, it said. With the war well into its fourth year, “a robust war economy and steady supply of weapons and other external support enabled the parties to sustain fighting as the conflict continued to spread and evolve,” the report said. The conflict is exacting an “unbearable toll” on civilians, while the prospects for a ceasefire and a peaceful resolution to the conflict remain elusive, it said. Ali Muhammad Ali Abd al-Rahman, a Sudanese national, waits to hear the verdict of the International Criminal Court (ICC), in The Hague, on December 9, 2025. The International Criminal Court on December 9, 2025, handed down a sentence of 20 years to a Sudanese militia leader for war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the country’s civil war two decades ago.
